newsitem.title: USA: Miami restaurant falls to Cuba exile politics.
newsitem.headline: Miami restaurant falls to Cuba exile politics.

text.p: A restaurant long at the heart of Cuban exile politics in Miami has closed its doors, a victim of -- exile politics, a newspaper said on Sunday.

Centro Vasco, a landmark eatery first opened in Havana and transplanted to Miami after Fidel Castro's revolution, closed on Saturday after 56 years in business, crushed by a political boycott over a Cuban entertainer, the Miami Herald reported Sunday.
The restaurant, in Miami's Little Havana, booked 73-year-old Cuban entertainer Rosita Fornes for a five-night run this summer.
Though the shows were sold out, Miami's strident Spanish language radio stations began a campaign against her appearance because the singer had never publicly repudiated Castro.
Boycotts and demonstrations followed. A Molotov cocktail was thrown through the restaurant's window. The shows were cancelled.
The community pressure became too much and the restaurant was put up for sale. The new owner planned to remodel and change the name.
Centro Vasco was opened in 1940 in Cuba by Spaniard Juan Saizarbitoria and moved to Miami in 1961, where it became a haunt for Cuban exile leaders who opposed the Castro regime.

"Every major exile organisation was formed here," Mirentxu Saizarbitoria, the current owner's daughter, told the Herald. "If anybody would understand that we would never to anything to hurt the community, it would be them. It's bizarre. It's been a mental deflowering."
